title: Induction Packet: Closed Asymmetry Atom to Domain-Specific Atomic Value

status.reason: The proposal is coherent with the current vertical-bar and projection framework, but the projection map, codomain, invariants, and uniqueness conditions are not yet formally defined or validated.

purpose: Induct the newly clarified distinction between a closed RT atomic unit and its projected atomic value, using (2|4) as the canonical working example and Euclidean side-value a as the initial target projection.

governed_existing_commitments.claim: The vertical bar | is the primitive admissible participation separator.
| is not ordinary division, a static ratio, mere punctuation, or set separation.
A|B is order-sensitive unless orientation reversal is explicitly proven.
A bar expression does not assert realized truth merely by being written; it becomes active under D or another registered comparison context.
Distance is to be recovered as a projection of deviation, and geometry as a projection of organized distance, without reintroducing geometry as primitive.

atomicity_claim.statement: (2|4) is one closed atomic RT unit whose meaning belongs to the whole bar-conditioned relation, not independently to 2 or 4.
atomicity_claim.clarification: The operands remain distinguishable as ordered participants, but they do not independently constitute the realized truth of Asym.

asymmetry_claim.statement: (2|4) is the closed relational realization of the whole truth of [Asym] for the declared symmetry references.

value_claim.statement: The atomic RT unit is not internally reduced to an untyped scalar. An atomic scalar value arises only through a declared domain projection.

types.alpha_L: ordinal relation of Asym relative to R_L
types.alpha_R: ordinal relation of Asym relative to R_R
types.Atom_RT: closed, ordered, admissibly evaluated RT atom
types.V_X: atomic value type admitted by target domain X

formal_candidate.non_identity_rule: a is not identical to 2, 4, 2/4, 4-2, 2+4, or any other scalarization unless that exact map is separately declared and justified as Pi_Euclid.
formal_candidate.information_rule: Projection may suppress relational information. Therefore Pi_X need not be invertible.
formal_candidate.context_rule: The same RT atom may lawfully project to different values in different domains only through separately typed projection maps.

semantic_distinctions.definition: An ordered participant presented to the primitive bar operator.
An order-sensitive admissible participation expression A|B awaiting or undergoing registered evaluation.
The evaluated and closed whole produced from the bar-conditioned participation relation.
A domain-typed value yielded by projecting the closed RT atom into a declared target domain.
A typed map from an RT atom to a domain representation; it is not an ontological replacement of the RT atom.

prohibited_interpretations: (2|4) is merely the Cartesian ordered pair (2,4).
The value a is automatically equal to 2, 4, 6, 2/4, 4/2, or |4-2|.
Projection proves ontological identity between the RT atom and its domain value.
The current proposal already derives the Pythagorean theorem.
Euclidean distance is being introduced as an RT primitive.

target_application.research_question: What lawful projection Pi_Euclid maps the closed RT asymmetry atom to a Euclidean side-length value a?
target_application.non_claim: No claim is made that the Pythagorean theorem is false, incomplete, supported, opposed, or replaced. The target is the RT antecedent and lawful emergence of its atomic side value a.

formal_obligations.task: Define the exact closure operator or closure predicate that licenses (2|4) as Atom_RT after bar evaluation.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: A typed rule distinguishes unevaluated 2|4 from closed (2|4)_RT.

formal_obligations.task: Define the operand types of 2 and 4 as ordinal relational indices rather than untyped natural numbers.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: The same numeral cannot silently change reference or type.

formal_obligations.task: Define Pi_Euclid and its codomain Length_Euclid.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: The projection returns one nonnegative Euclidean length value with declared units or a dimensionless normalized length.

formal_obligations.task: State which properties of (2|4)_RT are preserved under Pi_Euclid.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: At minimum, admissibility, orientation dependence, and nonnegative realized effect are explicitly accepted, transformed, or rejected.

formal_obligations.task: Determine whether Pi_Euclid is unique, context-indexed, or one member of an admissible projection family.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: Competing scalarizations cannot all be called a without a selection law.

formal_obligations.task: Define equivalence conditions for RT atoms that project to the same Euclidean value.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: Projection degeneracy is distinguished from RT identity.
The relationship between Pi_Euclid((2|4)_RT) and Pi_Euclid((4|2)_RT) is explicitly determined rather than assumed.

formal_obligations.task: Connect alpha indexing to the existing delta-alpha notation without conflating ordinal position with magnitude.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: alpha has one governed type and delta-alpha has a separately defined action.

formal_obligations.task: Show how three projected side values a, b, and c arise from three distinct or coupled RT atoms before testing a^2+b^2=c^2.
formal_obligations.success_criterion: The theorem-level test does not begin from undeclared scalar primitives.

candidate_axioms_or_definitions.text: A closed RT atom is an admissibly evaluated, order-preserving bar-conditioned whole. Its truth is attributed to the whole expression and not to either operand in isolation.
A domain projection Pi_X maps a closed RT atom to a value typed by domain X while preserving only the invariants explicitly declared for Pi_X.
An atomic domain value is the irreducible output of a registered projection in its target domain; it is not the internal scalar reduction of the source RT atom.
For an admissible closed asymmetry atom (m|n)_RT and a declared domain X, there may exist a lawful projection Pi_X((m|n)_RT)=v_X.

falsification_conditions: No typed distinction can be maintained between an unevaluated bar expression and a closed RT atom.
The value of Pi_Euclid depends on arbitrary notation changes rather than relational structure.
Orientation reversal produces contradictions with the declared order sensitivity of |.
No invariant projection rule can map equivalent RT cases consistently.
The construction requires Euclidean distance to be assumed before it is projected.
Two identical governed inputs and contexts yield incompatible atomic values without a declared nondeterministic rule.

recommended_validation_campaign.goal: Determine whether a closed bar-conditioned RT atom can lawfully and non-arbitrarily project to an atomic Euclidean value.

target_sections: Vertical Bar Operator: Admissible Participation Separator
induction_patch.proposed_heading: Closed Relational Atoms and Domain-Projected Atomic Values
proposed_text: A numerically instantiated bar expression such as 2|4 is not interpreted as ordinary division, a static ratio, or a Cartesian pair. Its operands denote ordered relational indices relative to declared reference conditions.
When the expression is admissibly evaluated and closed, (2|4)_RT is treated provisionally as one atomic relational unit realizing the whole truth of the corresponding asymmetry condition.
The closed atom is not internally reduced to an untyped scalar. A scalar or other domain-atomic value may arise only through a registered projection Pi_X: Atom_RT -> V_X.

For the Euclidean target, Pi_Euclid((2|4)_RT)=a is admitted only as a provisional research schema. The definition, uniqueness, invariants, units, and falsification conditions of Pi_Euclid remain open.
This schema does not alter or challenge the Pythagorean theorem. It seeks the RT antecedent of the theorem's side-value symbols before theorem-level relations are evaluated.

instructions: Compare every proposed statement against the newest available mono_process_textbook_complete.md.
Preserve the existing governed semantics of the vertical bar operator.
Do not reinterpret | as division, ratio, punctuation, tuple construction, or scalar subtraction.
Identify notation collisions, especially alpha, a, A, E, Asym, D, Pi, <S>, and >S<.
Produce exact patch locations and a human-facing summary.
Do not modify the SSOT automatically unless explicit write authority is separately supplied.
